must_find.note: gather without return_exceptions: one failed put kills the drain, await drain re-raises, gap-fill never runs, so the spec's failed-write retry is unreachable (not planted; both old and new runs found and proved it)

released check lives only in _fill_gaps; _write_artifact, the sink both the drain and gap-fill use, has none, so any future path that enqueues a released conversation again overwrites a good artifact with an empty one. Floored at P2 even with no such caller today
id() set relies on the runner returning every conversation it reported; runner.py drops retried attempts, so their ids can be reused by a later object and gap-fill raises for a scenario never written
runner reports every retry attempt; two attempts of one scenario can land in one batch and gather writes scenario-i.json twice concurrently, so the failed attempt's transcript can win
one index mismatch raises and fails the whole step, discarding every valid key already written
gather over the whole drained batch keeps every transcript and serialized body resident until the slowest put returns
PR claims memory is bounded by in-flight writes; the batch gather makes it bounded by burst size
docstring says the callback runs via asyncio.to_thread on an inner loop; the code is single-loop, and the release is only safe because of that
